observations: No new photos were provided after the seller’s reply.
The only visual evidence remains photo 0 showing a solar panel array; no battery/inverter/charge controller details are visible.

claims.claim: I tested it myself yesterday, everything I said is true.
claims.evidence: No test report/video or photos were provided to verify the battery/inverter/charge performance claims.

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours. Never repaired.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not show the battery or any label/serial/condition indicators.

risks.risk: Seller’s “everything I said is true” cannot be verified remotely without the actual battery/inverter/charge controller being shown and/or test evidence.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video: battery voltage before/after charging and during a controlled load test (or a meter reading screenshot), plus clear battery label (brand/model/capacity).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven (worst-case): battery treated as unknown/possibly not meeting the 8-hour claim; panels treated as generic/unknown wattage.

risks.risk: Panel wattage/model and quantity are still not readable/confirmed, so total value is unknown.
risks.proof: Request close-up of panel nameplate/label (brand, model, rated W) and a wide shot showing the full count in the frame.
risks.if_unproven: Price for the minimum visible quantity and lowest plausible wattage until confirmed.

risks.risk: Condition (cracks, delamination, water ingress) can’t be assessed from the single image.
risks.proof: Request close-ups of panel corners/edges and the glass surface under light (including any defects).
risks.if_unproven: Price as used/possibly imperfect condition (worst-case) until defect-free condition is shown.

proof_requests: Send clear photos of the exact battery being sold: brand/model label, capacity (Ah/Wh), and terminal area.
Send a short video test: show battery voltage readings and a discharge/load test that supports the “8 hours” statement (or provide a written test result screenshot).
Send close-up photos of panel nameplates showing brand/model and rated wattage (W), plus a wide shot confirming total panel count.
If an inverter/charge controller is included, send photos of their front labels/model numbers. (If not included, confirm explicitly.)
response.reason: The seller asserts the claims are true, but without new photos or test evidence, the battery/inverter details and the “8 hours / never repaired” statements remain unverified. With only photo 0 (panels, unreadable specs), a reliable worst-case price can’t be set.
